content.content: Every recorded change's diff touches only paths its own node owns. Ownership is therefore exclusive: a path has at most one owning node across the whole graph, and a path that two node documents both list is a violation rather than an arrangement the check resolves. A recorded diff that touches a path its own node does not own, and a path whose ownership two nodes both assert, are what the check reports: it names the path and the changes that disagree about it and stops there — no edit is moved to a more plausible owner, no change is rewritten, and no node document is amended so that the diff would fit. The check reports one thing more on the same terms: a node document that lists a path whose normal form leaves the repository. A listed path is read in normal form, and a normal form in which a `..` remains after every `..` is folded against the ordinary component before it is not ownable and contributes no owned path — both fixed by xzxtxymq and taken here as given, so such a listing sits outside the two report cases above without the check falling out of line with the owning set. What this decision adds is that the listing is reported rather than passed over: the report names the change whose document lists the path and the path, and stops there. It is a finding, not a repair — the node document is not amended and the listing is not dropped, and no change is moved or rewritten so that the listing would fit, because a report that repaired what it reported would assert a state it had already fixed. The owning set is taken as given from xzxtxymq, which fixes it exactly; this adds the check over what changes actually recorded, the exclusivity that follows, and the escaping listing, and adds no condition to which paths a change owns. Absolute paths, symlinks and case are outside this decision, which says nothing about whether they are owned.
content.rationale: The owning set is a definition, and a definition nothing confronts with history is only an intention: every guard attributes file state through ownership — recording places an edit by it, removal frees a change's paths by it, an inverse is taken over it — so a recorded diff that strays outside its own node's set corrupts the one-change-one-node mapping those guards read, and corrupts it silently. The place is after xzxtxymq because that decision fixes the owning set exactly; this one asks only whether what history recorded stayed inside it, so it takes the set as given rather than restating it, and one authority for ownership is what keeps attribution from having two rules to drift between. Fixing the normal form of a listed path also fixes its residue, and the residue is the case this refine must not lose: a `..` left after folding names no file in the repository, so a document listing it contributes no owned path and is neither a diff outside a set nor two nodes asserting one path — it would pass as clean while the check stayed perfectly aligned. Reporting it therefore costs no rule: the check names the change whose document lists the path and the path, using the owning set the prerequisite fixed rather than deciding the escape itself, and stops there — a finding, not a repair, on exactly the line this decision already draws for a diff that strays outside its set. What it refuses: a second ownership rule, so the check may never decide for itself which paths a change owns, and a path two nodes list is the violation rather than a tie it breaks; admitting an escaping normal form to an owned set, which would re-decide the prerequisite rather than use it; a silent skip, since a change or path the check cannot attribute is not thereby clean; and repair, because moving the edit, rewriting the change, amending the node document or dropping the listing would leave a report asserting a disagreement it had already removed. Absolute paths, symlinks and case are left where the prerequisite left them; this decision judges nothing about them. The seam-level read of the recorded changes belongs to the node that follows this one in this layer; the report's line form and the caller's status belong to the decisions that already settle them.
